item.content:encoded:
The Allan Gray Scholarship Programme for Entrepreneurial Development 2026 is an opportunity for academically capable, financially deserving Grade 6 learners in South Africa who demonstrate curiosity, entrepreneurial potential and a desire to create value in their communities.

Offered by the Allan Gray Orbis Foundation, the programme goes beyond conventional financial assistance. Successful scholars receive support to attend leading partner high schools while also gaining access to mentorship, entrepreneurial development, leadership opportunities, workshops, online learning and a community of like-minded young people.

The programme is designed to identify promising young learners at an early stage and give them the educational environment, resources and developmental support needed to grow their academic abilities and entrepreneurial potential.

The Foundation’s current information confirms that the 2026 application deadline is 15 September 2026. Applications posted after 15 September 2026 will not be considered.

Opportunity Overview

  • Opportunity: Allan Gray Scholarship Programme for Entrepreneurial Development
  • Category: High School Scholarship
  • Provider: Allan Gray Orbis Foundation
  • Target group: Current Grade 6 learners
  • Country: South Africa
  • Citizenship requirement: South African citizenship
  • Age requirement: Applicants must be 11 or 12 years old in Grade 6
  • Eligible birth years: 2014 or 2015
  • Academic requirement: Minimum 70% in English and Mathematics
  • Financial requirement: Applicants must demonstrate financial need
  • Application status: Applications are currently open
  • Application deadline: 15 September 2026
  • Programme focus: Education, entrepreneurship, leadership and personal development
  • Application methods: Online application and application form, subject to the Foundation’s submission requirements

About the Allan Gray Scholarship Programme

The Allan Gray Scholarship Programme is designed for young learners who demonstrate more than academic ability. The Foundation seeks learners with a curious and entrepreneurial mindset, the potential to excel academically and a genuine financial need.

Rather than treating a scholarship simply as a means of paying school fees, the programme takes a long-term approach to developing young people.

Scholars are introduced to entrepreneurial thinking, leadership, collaboration, problem-solving and value creation while continuing their formal high school education.

The programme is part of the Allan Gray Orbis Foundation’s broader commitment to identifying and developing entrepreneurial potential in Southern Africa. The Foundation describes entrepreneurship as an important avenue for creating meaningful employment and contributing to social and economic transformation.

What Makes This Scholarship Different?

Many scholarships focus primarily on academic funding. The Allan Gray Scholarship Programme takes a more holistic approach.

Successful scholars can receive financial assistance for their schooling while simultaneously participating in developmental interventions intended to strengthen their confidence, leadership abilities, entrepreneurial thinking and personal growth.

The Foundation’s model combines:

  1. Academic support
  2. Financial assistance
  3. Entrepreneurial development
  4. Mentorship
  5. Leadership development
  6. Peer learning
  7. Online learning
  8. Workshops and seminars
  9. Community engagement
  10. Exposure to entrepreneurship and value creation

This approach means that scholars are not simply supported through high school; they are introduced to a developmental environment intended to prepare them for future opportunities.

Who Can Apply?

The scholarship is specifically designed for young learners currently in Grade 6.

Applicants must meet the Foundation’s eligibility conditions before submitting an application.

1. Current Grade 6 Learner

The applicant must be a current Grade 6 learner in 2026.

This is an important requirement because the scholarship is intended to support learners transitioning from primary school into high school.

2. South African Citizenship

The applicant must be a South African citizen.

This means the programme is not a general international scholarship and is not open to applicants from other African countries or other continents.

3. Age Requirement

Applicants must be:

  • At least 11 years old; and
  • Not older than 12 years old in Grade 6.

For the 2026 application cycle, eligible applicants should have been born in 2014 or 2015.

4. Academic Performance

Applicants must obtain a minimum of:

  • 70% in English
  • 70% in Mathematics

The academic requirement is intended to identify learners who have demonstrated the potential to succeed in a demanding high-school environment.

5. Financial Need

Applicants must demonstrate that they are financially deserving.

Financial need is an important part of the selection process because the programme is intended to provide educational opportunities to learners who may otherwise face financial barriers to accessing leading high schools.

Applicants and their parents or legal guardians should therefore pay close attention to the financial documentation requested as part of the application.

Entrepreneurial Potential Is Important

The Allan Gray Scholarship is not simply a traditional academic scholarship.

The Foundation is looking for young people who demonstrate qualities associated with an entrepreneurial mindset.

These may include:

  • Curiosity
  • Initiative
  • Problem-solving ability
  • Leadership potential
  • Desire to create value
  • Positive attitude
  • Growth mindset
  • Willingness to collaborate
  • Interest in entrepreneurship
  • Ability to think creatively
  • Confidence and willingness to learn

A learner does not necessarily have to already own a business to demonstrate entrepreneurial potential.

The programme is intended to cultivate and develop entrepreneurial thinking, allowing young people to understand how they can identify problems, develop ideas, create value and contribute positively to society.

What Does the Allan Gray Scholarship Cover?

One of the strongest aspects of the opportunity is the breadth of support available to successful scholars.

1. Tuition and Boarding

The scholarship provides support for tuition and boarding, helping successful learners attend participating leading high schools without carrying the normal financial burden associated with these expenses.

2. Monthly Allowance

Scholars receive a monthly allowance, providing additional financial support during their studies.

3. Toiletries and Clothing

The scholarship also provides support for essential personal items, including:

  • Toiletries
  • School uniforms
  • Casual clothing

4. Extra-Mural Activities

Support is provided for extra-mural activities, enabling scholars to participate in activities outside the traditional classroom environment.

This can contribute to personal development, teamwork, confidence and leadership.

5. Stationery and Textbooks

The scholarship covers educational materials such as:

  • Stationery
  • Textbooks

This ensures that scholars have important resources needed for their academic work.

Entrepreneurial and Personal Development Benefits

Financial assistance is only one component of the programme.

The Foundation also provides a range of developmental opportunities designed to help scholars become confident and entrepreneurial young people.

Workshops

Scholars participate in workshops that expose them to concepts and experiences beyond their normal school curriculum.

Annual Entrepreneurial Conference

Participants have access to an annual entrepreneurial conference, providing exposure to entrepreneurial ideas, speakers, learning experiences and other participants.

Online Learning Campus

Scholars receive access to an Online Learning Campus, allowing them to participate in digital learning and development opportunities.

Programme Officer Mentorship

Each scholar can benefit from guidance and mentorship from a dedicated Programme Officer.

Mentorship is intended to help learners navigate their personal and developmental journey while encouraging them to explore their potential.

Like-Minded Community

Scholars become part of a community of young people who share an interest in learning, leadership, entrepreneurship and personal development.

This environment can encourage collaboration, peer learning and long-term relationships.

Skills and Qualities Scholars Can Develop

Through the combination of financial support, education and entrepreneurial development, the programme aims to help participants develop several important qualities.

Confidence

Young people are encouraged to develop greater confidence in their abilities, ideas and potential.

Entrepreneurial Mindset

Scholars learn to think differently about challenges, opportunities and value creation.

Growth Mindset

The programme encourages learners to view learning and development as an ongoing process.

Leadership

Participants are exposed to experiences designed to strengthen leadership qualities and their ability to positively influence others.

Problem-Solving

Entrepreneurial development encourages learners to identify challenges and think about possible solutions.

Collaboration

The programme places emphasis on community and collaboration, helping scholars understand the importance of working with others.

Mentorship and Development

Mentorship is an important part of the Allan Gray approach.

The Foundation combines face-to-face learning, online learning, peer learning and individual interventions to nurture the potential already demonstrated by participating learners.

Rather than expecting a young person to develop independently, the programme provides structured support throughout the scholar’s journey.

This can help learners develop a stronger understanding of entrepreneurship while also building confidence and leadership skills.

How the Application and Selection Process Works

Applicants should understand that submitting an application does not automatically guarantee a scholarship.

The selection process involves several stages.

Step 1: Submit the Application

Applicants must submit the required application form together with the necessary supporting documentation.

The Foundation provides an online application option as well as an official application form.

Applicants should ensure that all required sections are completed correctly and that the requested supporting documents are included.

Step 2: Foundation Assessment

Successful applicants will be required to write a Foundation assessment in English and Mathematics at Grade 6 level in December 2026.

This assessment forms part of the selection process.

Step 3: Interviews

After the Foundation assessment, successful candidates will be invited to interviews in early 2027.

The interviews provide an opportunity for the selection team to learn more about candidates beyond their academic results.

Step 4: Placement School Interviews

Recommended candidates will subsequently be invited to participating placement schools for interviews.

This means that selection involves both the Foundation and the relevant school.

Step 5: Scholarship Award

Candidates whose recommendations are approved by the placement schools will be awarded the Allan Gray Scholarship.

According to the programme information, scholarship awards are expected in May 2027.

Step 6: Memorandum of Agreement

Once the scholarship has been awarded, the Foundation, placement school and the scholar’s custodian will sign a Memorandum of Agreement.

This formalises the scholarship arrangement and the responsibilities of the relevant parties.

Important Documents and Application Requirements

Applicants should carefully review the official application form before submitting their application.

The 2026 application documentation states that applicants must provide supporting academic documentation, including certified copies of the applicant’s Grade 5 fourth-term report and Grade 6 second-term report. The reports must show the applicant’s name, grade and school. Failure to provide the required documentation can result in automatic disqualification.

Parents or legal guardians should also provide an active cellphone number and valid email address because these may be used for communication concerning the application.

The Foundation’s 2026 application form also states that faxed and emailed copies of the application form will not be accepted. Applicants should therefore follow the official submission instructions carefully rather than simply emailing their completed documents.

Application Deadline

The deadline for the 2026 Allan Gray Scholarship Programme is 15 September 2026.

The official 2026 application form specifically states that application forms posted after 15 September 2026 will not be considered.

Applicants should not wait until the final day to begin the application process.

Parents and guardians should allow sufficient time to:

  1. Review the eligibility criteria.
  2. Obtain the application form.
  3. Gather supporting documentation.
  4. Obtain certified copies where required.
  5. Complete the application accurately.
  6. Ensure that the form is properly signed.
  7. Submit the application according to the official instructions.
  8. Allow sufficient time for postal delivery where applicable.

Who Should Consider Applying?

This opportunity may be particularly suitable for a Grade 6 learner who:

  • Performs strongly in Mathematics and English.
  • Is curious and eager to learn.
  • Shows interest in entrepreneurship or business.
  • Demonstrates leadership potential.
  • Enjoys solving problems.
  • Has ideas and enjoys finding ways to improve things.
  • Wants to develop confidence.
  • Is willing to work with other young people.
  • Comes from a financially deserving household.
  • Wants to attend a leading high school.
  • Is interested in developing an entrepreneurial mindset from an early age.

Parents and guardians should also consider whether the learner is comfortable participating in assessments, interviews, mentorship, workshops and other programme activities.

Why Parents and Guardians Should Pay Attention to This Opportunity

For a financially deserving learner, gaining access to a high-quality high-school environment can have a significant impact on educational and personal development.

The Allan Gray Scholarship Programme goes further by combining school support with entrepreneurial development.

A successful scholar can therefore receive assistance with important educational and living costs while also gaining exposure to:

  • Mentorship
  • Entrepreneurship
  • Leadership
  • Personal development
  • Workshops
  • Conferences
  • Online learning
  • Peer learning
  • Collaboration
  • Speakers and seminars
  • A community of like-minded young people

The Foundation’s wider work also places significant emphasis on developing entrepreneurial potential early. Its Scholarship Programme has supported hundreds of young people and places scholars in partner schools where academic development is combined with personal and entrepreneurial development.

Important Application Advice

Start Early

Do not wait until the deadline before gathering documents.

Some supporting documents may take time to obtain, particularly certified copies.

Check the Academic Requirements

Make sure the learner meets the minimum 70% requirement for English and Mathematics before applying.

Complete the Application Carefully

Incorrect, incomplete or missing information can negatively affect an application.

Prepare the Supporting Documents

Review the official application form carefully and ensure that all required documentation is attached.

Pay Attention to Submission Instructions

The Foundation’s 2026 form specifically states that faxed and emailed application forms will not be accepted. Follow the official submission process provided by the Foundation.

Keep Copies of Submitted Documents

Parents or guardians should retain copies of the completed application and supporting documentation for their own records.

Monitor Communication Channels

Make sure the contact information provided is active and regularly monitored because the Foundation may use the supplied cellphone number and email address to communicate with applicants.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should use the official Allan Gray Orbis Foundation application channels.

Online Application:
Apply Online through Allan Gray Orbis Foundation

Application Form:
Download the 2026 Allan Gray Scholarship Application Form

Applicants and parents or guardians should rely on the official Foundation instructions for the most accurate information regarding submission requirements and procedures.

More information, visit the school website HERE

Visit the OFY Website HERE for more scholarships

Key Facts at a Glance

Detail Information
Programme Allan Gray Scholarship Programme for Entrepreneurial Development
Provider Allan Gray Orbis Foundation
Level High School
Target learner Current Grade 6 learner
Citizenship South African citizen
Age 11–12 years
Birth years for 2026 2014 or 2015

Mathematics requirement Minimum 70%

Boarding Covered

Toiletries Covered

Stationery and textbooks Covered
Mentorship Provided
Workshops Included

Foundation assessment December 2026
Interviews Early 2027
Expected scholarship award May 2027

Conclusion

The Allan Gray Scholarship Programme for Entrepreneurial Development 2026 presents a comprehensive educational opportunity for eligible South African Grade 6 learners who demonstrate academic potential, entrepreneurial curiosity and financial need.

The programme is particularly valuable because it does not stop at paying for education. Successful scholars can receive support for tuition, boarding, clothing, toiletries, textbooks, stationery, extra-mural activities and a monthly allowance while also gaining access to mentorship, workshops, entrepreneurial conferences, online learning and a community of like-minded young people.

The long-term objective is to help young learners develop into confident individuals who can think entrepreneurially, solve problems, create value, collaborate with others and demonstrate leadership.

Eligible families should begin preparing their applications early and carefully follow the official submission requirements. With the 15 September 2026 deadline approaching, applicants should ensure that their forms and supporting documentation are complete and submitted through the approved channels before the closing date.

For the official programme information and application materials, visit the Allan Gray Orbis Foundation and use the official application channels provided above.

item.content:encoded:
The Wilson Center Congressional Fellowship Program (CFP) is a six-week professional development fellowship designed for current Congressional staff who want to deepen their understanding of global affairs, debate major foreign policy issues, and connect with leading experts and policymakers.

The programme brings together Congressional staffers from across the political aisle and creates an environment where participants can exchange ideas, examine complex international issues, and develop stronger professional networks.

About the Congressional Fellowship Program

The Wilson Center’s Congressional Fellowship Program focuses on foreign policy, global affairs and the legislative process.

Throughout the six-week seminar, Fellows engage with leading foreign policy thinkers and practitioners. Sessions are designed to encourage analytical thinking, fresh perspectives and informed debate around important international issues.

The programme also includes an interactive simulation intended to encourage Fellows from across the political aisle to network, collaborate and work together.

What Does the Fellowship Offer?

Selected Fellows will participate in a structured six-week seminar covering key global and foreign policy issues.

The programme provides opportunities to:

  • Debate major international and foreign policy issues.
  • Engage with leading foreign policy experts and practitioners.
  • Develop analytical approaches to complex global issues.
  • Gain fresh perspectives through discussions and recommended readings.
  • Network with Congressional staff from across the political aisle.
  • Participate in an interactive simulation.
  • Connect with policymakers, academics and executives through the Wilson Center community.

Certificate of Completion

Fellows are expected to attend the majority of the programme sessions.

Participants who attend at least five of the six sessions will receive a certificate of completion from the Wilson Center.

Successful Fellows will also become part of the Woodrow Wilson Congressional Fellowship Alumni Network.

Access to the Wilson Center Alumni Network

One of the long-term benefits of the programme is continued access to the Wilson Center’s alumni community.

The programme has an alumni network of approximately 1,000 members, providing Fellows with opportunities to maintain professional connections after completing the programme.

Alumni may also be invited to participate in exclusive Wilson Center opportunities, including:

  • Private briefings
  • Study trips around the world
  • High-level roundtables
  • Other Wilson Center events and activities

Alumni can also draw upon the expertise of Wilson Center experts, including policymakers, academics and executives from both the public and private sectors.

Who Is the Fellowship For?

The Congressional Fellowship Program is specifically designed for mid- to senior-level Congressional staff.

Applicants should:

  • Be current Congressional staff.
  • Have a strong understanding of the legislative process.
  • Have an interest in foreign policy.
  • Aspire to pursue or continue a career focused on shaping foreign policy.
  • Be able to attend at least five of the six required sessions.

The programme is therefore not presented as a general fellowship open to students, recent graduates or members of the general public.

Programme Schedule

The provided information lists the following six sessions:

  1. September 18
  2. September 25
  3. October 2
  4. October 16
  5. October 23
  6. October 30

The sessions take place on Fridays from 2:30 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. at the Wilson Center or on Capitol Hill.

Applicants should only apply if they are confident that they can meet the required attendance commitment.

Spring and Fall Sessions

The Wilson Center states that it hosts two Congressional Fellowship Program sessions each year, one in the spring and one in the fall.

The provided announcement states that applications for the Fall 2026 session are now open. It also contains a separate reference stating that applications for Spring 2026 are open. Because the supplied information contains both references, applicants should check the official application page for the session and dates currently accepting applications.

How to Apply

Interested Congressional staff should submit their application through the Wilson Center’s application portal.

APPLY HERE

Applicants should carefully review the programme requirements and make sure they can attend the required sessions before applying.

Application Deadline

The information provided does not specify an application deadline for the Fall 2026 session.

Applicants should therefore check the official application page for the current deadline and any additional application requirements before submitting their application.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Wilson Center Congressional Fellowship Program 2026

Conclusion

The Wilson Center Congressional Fellowship Program provides current Congressional staff with an opportunity to strengthen their understanding of foreign policy while engaging directly with experts, policymakers and fellow Congressional professionals.

Through its six-week seminar, interactive discussions, cross-aisle networking and alumni opportunities, the programme can help Congressional staff develop the knowledge and professional relationships needed to contribute more effectively to foreign policy discussions.

However, applicants should note that the programme is specifically intended for current Congressional staff, particularly those at the mid- to senior-level who have an understanding of the legislative process and an interest in shaping foreign policy..

item.content:encoded:
The Pinterest Apprenticeship Program provides professionals from non-technical backgrounds and individuals who may face barriers to entering the technology industry with an opportunity to gain practical experience at Pinterest.

The programme is designed for people looking to transition into technology while gaining hands-on experience in areas including engineering, product management, product design and product research.

About the Pinterest Apprenticeship Program

Entering the technology industry can be difficult for people who did not begin their careers in traditional technology roles. Pinterest’s apprenticeship programme provides an alternative pathway for professionals who want to develop relevant skills and gain experience within a technology company.

The programme specifically aims to support people from non-tech backgrounds and individuals who may have experienced barriers to entering the industry.

Rather than requiring everyone to follow the same traditional career path, the programme creates opportunities across several areas of technology and product development.

Apprenticeship Opportunities Available

The Pinterest Apprenticeship Program features four main pathways:

1. Apprentice Engineer

The Apprentice Engineer pathway provides an opportunity to gain experience in software engineering and technology development.

Depending on the position, apprentices may be exposed to:

  • Software development
  • Engineering projects
  • Technical problem-solving
  • Working with engineering teams
  • Development processes
  • Technology products and systems

This pathway can be suitable for professionals who have developed technical skills through alternative education or career routes and want to transition into a professional engineering environment.

2. Apprentice Product Manager

The Apprentice Product Manager pathway focuses on developing and improving digital products.

Product management involves understanding user needs, identifying opportunities and working with different teams to guide product development.

Apprentices may gain experience in:

  • Product strategy
  • User needs and research
  • Product development
  • Cross-functional collaboration
  • Problem identification
  • Product decision-making

This pathway may be particularly relevant to people with backgrounds in business, strategy, communications, project management or research.

3. Apprentice Product Designer

The Apprentice Product Designer pathway focuses on creating digital products and user experiences.

Participants may gain experience in:

  • Digital product design
  • User experience
  • User interface design
  • Design thinking
  • Problem-solving
  • Working with product and engineering teams

This can provide an entry point into technology for professionals with design or other creative backgrounds.

4. Apprentice Product Researcher

The Apprentice Product Researcher pathway focuses on understanding users and using research findings to inform product decisions.

Areas of exposure may include:

  • User research
  • Research methodologies
  • User behaviour
  • Data and insights
  • Product decision-making
  • Collaboration with designers, engineers and product managers

This pathway may be relevant to people with backgrounds in research, psychology, sociology, social sciences, communications and related disciplines.

APPY HERE

How Long Does the Apprenticeship Last?

Pinterest states that apprenticeships can last for up to one year. However, the exact length of an apprenticeship is not guaranteed.

Participants are employed throughout the programme, and apprentices may potentially be considered for conversion to a full-time role at Pinterest after completing the apprenticeship.

It is important to note that full-time employment is not guaranteed.

Who Is the Programme Designed For?

The programme is particularly focused on:

  • Professionals from non-tech backgrounds
  • Individuals seeking to transition into technology
  • People who may have experienced barriers to entering the technology industry
  • Candidates interested in engineering, product management, product design or product research
  • Individuals looking for an alternative pathway into the technology sector

This makes the programme especially interesting for career changers who already possess transferable skills but need practical technology industry experience.

What Can Apprentices Gain?

An apprenticeship can provide an opportunity to develop both technical and professional capabilities while working in a real-world environment.

Participants can potentially build:

  • Industry knowledge
  • Technical and professional skills
  • Practical work experience
  • Professional networks
  • Understanding of technology development
  • Confidence working with cross-functional teams

These experiences can help participants become better prepared for future technology roles.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Pinterest Apprenticeship Program

Potential Pathway to Full-Time Employment

One of the major attractions of the programme is the possibility of being considered for a full-time position at Pinterest.

However, applicants should understand that conversion is not guaranteed.

The apprenticeship should therefore be viewed primarily as a professional development and work experience opportunity, with potential for longer-term employment depending on available roles and the individual’s performance.

A Supportive Professional Community

Pinterest also highlights its focus on building a community where employees can develop relationships, connections and a sense of belonging.

For apprentices, being surrounded by colleagues and professionals can be particularly valuable when making a career transition into a new industry.

How to Prepare for the Programme

Although the next application opening has not been given a specific deadline, prospective applicants can start preparing now.

1. Choose Your Career Path

Consider whether you are most interested in:

  • Engineering
  • Product management
  • Product design
  • Product research

2. Highlight Transferable Skills

Coming from a non-tech background does not mean you have no relevant experience.

Skills such as communication, research, problem-solving, project management, data analysis, creativity, business strategy, customer understanding and leadership can be valuable in technology roles.

3. Build Relevant Projects

Start creating evidence of your skills.

For example:

  • Engineering candidates can build software projects.
  • Product management candidates can create product case studies.
  • Designers can develop UX/UI portfolios.
  • Product researchers can showcase research projects and user insights.

4. Research Pinterest

Learn about Pinterest’s products, users and technology. Understanding the company’s platform can help demonstrate genuine interest when applications open.

5. Sign Up for Updates

Pinterest is encouraging interested candidates to sign up for apprenticeship notifications so they can receive updates when applications open for the next cohort.

Application Deadline

No specific application deadline has been announced for the next cohort.

Interested candidates should sign up for notifications and monitor Pinterest’s official apprenticeship channels for the next application opening.

Conclusion

The Pinterest Apprenticeship Program offers an alternative route into the technology industry for professionals who may not have followed a traditional technology career path.

item.content:encoded:
The Lawyers’ Committee for Civil Rights Under Law is inviting applications for an Externally Funded Fellowship 2027–2029 with its Digital Justice Initiative in Washington, DC.

This fellowship offers an exciting opportunity for an emerging legal professional committed to racial justice, civil rights, privacy, and emerging technology to work at the intersection of law and technology.

The fellow will have the opportunity to identify emerging legal and policy challenges while also developing strategies to hold corporate and government actors accountable through litigation and advocacy.

About the Digital Justice Initiative

The Digital Justice Initiative focuses on the intersection of racial justice, technology, and privacy.

The initiative addresses issues including exploitative data practices, discriminatory algorithms, privacy violations, disinformation, and online hate, particularly where these practices disproportionately affect communities of color.

Fellows will participate in substantive legal work, including co-counseled litigation with prominent law firms. Their responsibilities may include client contact, case investigation, discovery, negotiations, amicus briefs, appeals, and trial practice.

They may also contribute to legislative and public policy advocacy, legal services, and public education on civil rights issues.

Fellowship Focus Areas

The fellowship may focus on one of two primary areas:

1. Surveillance Pricing

The project may examine surveillance pricing including concerns surrounding data privacy, discrimination, and the collection and exploitation of sensitive personal information.

2. Generative AI

The fellow may explore discrimination in generative AI tools, expanding civil rights research beyond traditional algorithmic decision-making systems and examining how emerging AI technologies may affect communities of color.

The Lawyers’ Committee is also open to considering proposals that align with its mission and priorities but fall outside these specific focus areas.

What the Fellow Will Do

The selected fellow may:

* Conduct factual and legal research on relevant technologies and practices.
* Engage with affected communities, scholars, practitioners, and organizations.
* Help shape litigation and advocacy strategies.
* Develop cases challenging discriminatory practices.
* Participate in implementing strategies developed during the fellowship.
* Contribute to litigation and legal advocacy.
* Support public policy and legislative advocacy.
* Participate in public education on important civil rights issues.

Eligibility Requirements

Applicants should meet the following requirements:

* Hold a JD or anticipate receiving a JD by May 2027.
* Demonstrate a strong commitment to civil rights and racial justice.
* Demonstrate creativity and initiative in developing and implementing civil rights projects.
* Have prior experience working with or ties to low-income communities of color.
* Have strong research, writing, and analytical abilities.
* Be able to work collaboratively with staff, clients, and community organizations.
* Have effective written and oral communication skills in legal and non-legal settings.
* A computer science or other technology background is preferred.

Application Requirements

Interested candidates should submit:

* Project Proposal– Including the proposed project’s objectives, timeline, target populations, and expected outcomes.
* Resume
* Personal Statement – Describing relevant experience and qualifications.
* References – Contact information for at least two professional or academic references.

Salary and Benefits

The fellowship is externally funded and will commence only if outside fellowship funding is secured.

For an attorney receiving their JD in 2027, the expected salary is $76,000. If the external fellowship award is lower than the Lawyers’ Committee salary scale, the organization will provide an additional amount to bring the fellow up to the appropriate salary.

Benefits include:

* Medical, dental, and vision healthcare coverage
* Parental leave
* 403(b) employer contributions and matching
* Short- and long-term disability options
* Employer-paid monthly cell phone stipend

Fellowship Details

Position: Fellow
Programme: Digital Justice Initiative
Organization: Lawyers’ Committee for Civil Rights Under Law
Location: Washington, DC
Duration: 2027–2029

item.content:encoded:
The Department of Human Geography at Lund University is inviting applications for 1–2 PhD positions in Human/Economic Geography under the ERC-funded DECENT project (Socio-technical Modularity and the Decentralization of Infrastructure).

The selected PhD students will be employed within the DECENT project and affiliated with CIRCLE (Centre for Innovation Research). The positions are particularly suitable for candidates interested in economic geography, innovation studies, socio-technical transitions, sustainability transitions, geography of innovation, and urban experimentation.

About the DECENT Project

Cities have traditionally depended on centralised infrastructure systems to provide essential services such as electricity, water, transportation, food, and finance. However, large-scale network-based infrastructures can struggle to adequately address changing social, economic, and environmental needs.

The DECENT project examines how decentralized infrastructure solutions can provide societal functions in more modular ways.

Examples of decentralized infrastructure being studied include:

* Micro-grids
* Small-scale wastewater treatment systems
* Multi-modal transport
* Short food chains
* Distributed finance

The project investigates how these decentralized solutions can overcome the historical legacies of large-scale infrastructure systems.

Researchers will approach decentralization from a configurational socio-technical perspective, examining areas including local and global industry dynamics, the geography of innovation, sustainability transitions, and urban experimentation.

The empirical research will compare infrastructure decentralization across cities in both high-income regions, such as Europe and North America, and middle-income regions, including South and Southeast Asia.

PhD Research Opportunity

The positions are based within the Department of Human Geography at Lund University and form part of the interdisciplinary DECENT research project.

Successful candidates will have the opportunity to conduct doctoral research connected to the project’s broader themes while developing expertise in areas such as:

* Economic and human geography
* Innovation studies
* Socio-technical transitions
* Sustainability transitions
* Geography of innovation
* Urban experimentation
* Infrastructure decentralization
* Local and global industry dynamics

The positions may be particularly attractive to applicants interested in understanding how cities can transition from centralised infrastructure systems toward more distributed and modular alternatives.

Who Should Apply?

The opportunity is suitable for candidates with academic and research interests related to human geography, economic geography, innovation studies, socio-technical transitions, sustainability, infrastructure, cities, and urban development.

Applicants should carefully review the official vacancy announcement for the complete eligibility requirements, required qualifications, application documents, and other conditions of employment.

About Lund University

Lund University is a major research university in Sweden with a broad international research environment. The PhD students will be based in the Department of Human Geography and affiliated with CIRCLE, the Centre for Innovation Research.

Working within the DECENT project will provide doctoral researchers with an opportunity to contribute to research examining some of the major challenges surrounding infrastructure, innovation, sustainability, and urban transformation.

How to Apply

Interested candidates should review the full vacancy announcement and submit their application through Lund University’s official recruitment portal.

Number of Positions: 1–2 PhD positions
Field: Human/Economic Geography
Project: DECENT – Socio-technical Modularity and the Decentralization of Infrastructure
Funding: European Research Council (ERC)
Institution: Lund University, Sweden
Deadline: August 28, 2026

Application Link

Apply here: https://s-tep.org/job-opportunity-1-2-phd-positions-in-the-decent-project/

Applicants are encouraged to review the complete job description and application requirements before submitting their applications.

Conclusion

The DECENT PhD positions at Lund University offer an opportunity for aspiring researchers to contribute to an ERC-funded project exploring how cities can rethink the way essential services and infrastructure are organised.

Candidates interested in economic geography, innovation, sustainability transitions, socio-technical systems, and urban experimentation are encouraged to explore the opportunity and apply before the August 28, 2026 deadline. Discover more opportunities like this HERE.

item.content:encoded:
The Cherie Blair Foundation for Women has opened applications for a new 12-month mentoring cohort exclusively for women entrepreneurs in India. The programme offers selected women entrepreneurs the opportunity to work with an experienced business mentor who can provide guidance, expertise and support to help them develop their businesses and achieve their professional goals.

Through the Mentoring Women in Business programme, participants are matched with business professionals from around the world and work together online to identify goals, address business challenges, strengthen skills and develop practical strategies for business growth.

The programme is designed to provide women entrepreneurs with access to personalised mentoring, new perspectives, professional networks and valuable business knowledge.

About the Cherie Blair Foundation for Women Mentoring Programme

The Mentoring Women in Business programme is a global initiative of the Cherie Blair Foundation for Women that connects women entrepreneurs in low- and middle-income countries with experienced business professionals.

The programme is delivered online and provides one-to-one mentoring over 12 months. Mentees and mentors work together to create a plan focused on the entrepreneur’s business and personal development goals.

The Foundation reports that among mentees graduating in 2024, 99% gained business skills, 96% applied improved business management practices, 94% progressed towards their business objectives, and 86% improved their business outcomes.

What the Mentoring Programme Offers

Selected women entrepreneurs will have the opportunity to:

* Receive personalised one-to-one mentoring from an experienced business professional.
* Work on specific personal and business development goals.
* Strengthen business management and professional skills.
* Gain new perspectives and practical advice from their mentor.
* Build confidence in making business decisions.
* Expand their professional and business networks.
* Work through challenges affecting their business growth.
* Access the Foundation’s online mentoring platform and community.
* Receive support from the programme team throughout the mentoring relationship.
* Receive a certificate upon successful completion of the programme.

Eligibility Criteria

The opportunity is specifically open to women entrepreneurs based in India for this cohort.

Applicants should generally:

* Be a woman from and living in a low- or middle-income country.
* Own and run a business, with at least 51% ownership or decision-making authority, or be preparing to launch a business within the next three months.
* Have intermediate-level or higher proficiency in English, both written and spoken.
* Be able to commit to the programme for 12 months.
* Have reliable internet access and be able to meet with a mentor online.
* Be willing to work with a mentor to develop business and personal development skills.
* Complete the required training, feedback questionnaires and programme activities.
* Commit to meeting with their mentor for a minimum of two hours per month. ([Cherie Blair Foundation for Women]

How the Mentoring Works

Once selected, participants will complete approximately 1.5 hours of pre-matching training before being paired with a mentor.

The mentor and mentee will then work together through several stages, including getting to know one another, establishing goals, developing an action plan, working towards objectives and reflecting on progress.

Meetings take place online, with participants expected to spend at least two hours per month with their mentor. The programme team also provides ongoing support throughout the mentoring relationship. ([Cherie Blair Foundation for Women]

Who Should Apply?

This opportunity is ideal for women entrepreneurs in India who are looking to grow their businesses, strengthen their entrepreneurial skills, overcome business challenges and benefit from the experience of an international business professional.

Whether you are looking to improve your business strategy, strengthen your management skills, expand your network or work towards specific growth objectives, the mentoring relationship can provide personalised support throughout the year.

Application Process

Interested applicants should review the programme’s selection criteria and commitments before completing the online application form.

The application requires responses in English and takes approximately 15–20 minutes to complete, according to the Foundation’s programme information. ([Cherie Blair Foundation for Women]

How to Apply

Applications are currently being promoted for the India cohort.

Application Deadline: 4 September 2026

Applicants should complete the online application before the deadline and ensure that they meet all programme requirements.

Application Link: [Apply for the Cherie Blair Foundation Mentoring Programme]

For questions regarding the mentoring application, applicants can contact [mentoringintakes@cherieblairfoundation.org]

Conclusion

The Cherie Blair Foundation for Women Mentoring Women in Business programme provides women entrepreneurs with an opportunity to gain personalised guidance while working towards meaningful business and professional goals.

For eligible women entrepreneurs in India, this 12-month mentoring opportunity can provide access to international expertise, practical business support, professional networks and a community of ambitious entrepreneurs.

If you know a woman entrepreneur who is ready to take her business to the next level, encourage her to apply before the 4 September 2026 deadline.

Discover more opportunities like this on the OFY Webpage.

item.content:encoded:
The L’Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science International Awards 2027 celebrate outstanding women scientists whose research is making major contributions to the advancement of Physical Sciences, Mathematics and Computer Science.

Created in 1998, the International Awards are one of the flagship initiatives of the L’Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science programme. Every year, the programme honours five eminent women scientists from five regions of the world, recognising exceptional scientific achievement and the important role women play at the forefront of global research.

The scientific disciplines recognised by the International Awards alternate each year between Life Sciences and Physical Sciences, Mathematics and Computer Science. For the 2027 edition, the awards focus on Physical Sciences, Mathematics and Computer Science.

Each of the five selected laureates will receive an award of €100,000.

Please note that this opportunity is different from the L’Oréal-UNESCO regional fellowships and Young Talents programmes. The 2027 International Awards are intended to recognise established, internationally distinguished women scientists rather than doctoral students or early-career researchers.

About the L’Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science International Awards

The L’Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science programme was created to recognise the achievements of women researchers and increase the visibility of women in science.

Since the International Awards were launched in 1998, a total of 142 endowments have been awarded.

Through the programme, L’Oréal and UNESCO seek to highlight women whose scientific work has contributed significantly to knowledge, innovation and scientific progress.

For the 2027 cycle, the programme recognises excellence in:

  • Physical Sciences
  • Mathematics
  • Computer Science

Five women scientists will ultimately be selected, representing five major regions of the world.

Who Can Be Considered?

The International Awards are intended for eminent women scientists who have made important contributions to scientific advancement.

Unlike programmes designed specifically for PhD candidates, postdoctoral researchers or young scientists, the International Awards recognise highly accomplished researchers with significant scientific achievements.

Candidates should have an outstanding record of research in areas falling within the 2027 award disciplines:

Physical Sciences

Eligible research may fall within disciplines connected to the physical sciences and related fields covered under the programme’s official rules.

Mathematics

Women researchers whose work advances mathematical knowledge may be considered for the award.

Computer Science

Researchers making important contributions to computer science and related areas are also included in the 2027 scientific focus.

Applicants and nominators should consult the official 2027 Rules and Regulations to confirm whether a candidate’s specific scientific discipline falls within the eligible scope.

Five Global Laureates

One of the defining features of the L’Oréal-UNESCO International Awards is their global reach.

Each year, five laureates representing five regions of the world are selected.

The programme is therefore designed to recognise scientific excellence across different geographical regions and strengthen the international visibility of women researchers.

The five selected scientists will join an international community of previous L’Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science laureates.

Selection Process

Candidates are evaluated by a jury composed of internationally renowned scientific experts.

The International Awards place scientific excellence at the centre of the selection process.

The programme seeks women researchers whose work has made important contributions to scientific progress and who demonstrate the exceptional achievements associated with one of the world’s leading international recognitions for women in science.

According to the 2027 calendar, the final selection of candidates is expected to be completed by:

31 December 2026

What You Get

Each of the five selected laureates receives:

€100,000

The award also brings substantial international recognition through the global L’Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science programme.

Beyond the monetary endowment, recognition through the programme can provide greater international visibility for the scientific work and achievements of selected laureates.

The International Awards are designed to celebrate women working at the highest levels of scientific research and highlight their contributions to global scientific advancement.

Key Programme Information

Programme: L’Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science International Awards 2027

Scientific focus: Physical Sciences, Mathematics and Computer Science

Number of laureates: 5

Award per laureate: €100,000

Partner: UNESCO

Programme established: 1998

Total endowments awarded since launch: 142

Final selection: 31 December 2026

How to Apply or Nominate

Applications and nominations are managed through the official L’Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science platform.

To submit an application or nomination, users must:

  1. Create or log in to an account on the official For Women in Science platform.
  2. Access the relevant International Awards programme when the call is open.
  3. Follow the application or nomination instructions provided through the platform.
  4. Submit all required information and supporting documentation before the applicable deadline.

If a user is logged into the platform but cannot access the form, the programme advises consulting the “How do I apply for a program?” section of its FAQ.

Applicants and nominators should also review the official 2027 Rules and Regulations before preparing a submission.

APPLY HERE

Important Dates

The official calendar for the 2027 L’Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science International Awards in Physical Sciences, Mathematics and Computer Science is:

  • 6 April 2026: Call for applications/nominations opened
  • 5 July 2026: Call for applications/nominations closed
  • 31 December 2026: Final selection of candidates

Because the submission deadline was 5 July 2026, the nomination/application period for the 2027 International Awards is now closed.

Those interested in future editions should continue monitoring the official For Women in Science platform for the next call.

Important Clarification

The L’Oréal-UNESCO International Awards should not be confused with regional For Women in Science Fellowships or Young Talents programmes.

The International Awards:

  • Recognise five eminent women scientists globally
  • Provide €100,000 to each laureate
  • Focus on different scientific disciplines in alternating years
  • Are intended to honour significant, established scientific achievement

Regional fellowships may have different deadlines, eligibility requirements, award amounts and career-stage requirements.

For this reason, information relating to a 31 August 2026 deadline for a Sub-Saharan Africa fellowship should not be applied to the 2027 International Awards described in this article.

Why the L’Oréal-UNESCO International Awards Matter

Women continue to make groundbreaking contributions across mathematics, computing, physics and related scientific disciplines, yet their work has historically been underrepresented in some of the world’s most prominent scientific awards and leadership structures.

The L’Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science International Awards seek to increase the visibility of women researchers whose discoveries and ideas are helping push scientific boundaries forward.

By recognising five exceptional scientists each year, the programme celebrates not simply individual achievement but also the broader importance of ensuring that women can participate, lead and receive recognition at the highest levels of international science.

Final Thoughts

The L’Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science International Awards 2027 represent a prestigious global recognition for exceptional women scientists working in Physical Sciences, Mathematics and Computer Science.

Five laureates from five regions of the world will each receive €100,000, recognising scientific achievements that have contributed substantially to the progress of research.

The 2027 nomination cycle opened on 6 April 2026 and closed on 5 July 2026, with final selections expected by 31 December 2026.

Researchers, universities, scientific institutions and potential nominators interested in future editions should monitor the official L’Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science platform for upcoming calls.

For more information about this opportunity, VISIT HERE.

For more global opportunities, CLICK HERE.

item.content:encoded:
The University of Otago Doctoral Scholarship is one of the University of Otago’s principal funding opportunities for students undertaking doctoral research in New Zealand. The scholarship supports academically outstanding candidates with strong research potential who are seeking to complete a PhD or an eligible professional doctorate at the University.

For 2026, the scholarship provides a NZ$34,128 annual stipend, together with a tuition fee waiver at the domestic rate for up to 36 months of full-time doctoral study. The University indicates that up to 153 doctoral scholarships may be offered annually, making this one of its major postgraduate research funding programmes.

Applications can be submitted throughout the year through the University of Otago’s eVision student portal. Rather than operating with one annual deadline, applications are considered through quarterly selection rounds in March, June, September and November.

Applicants should note that the University of Otago is currently reviewing the strategic direction of its doctoral scholarship programme. Prospective candidates are therefore encouraged to check the official scholarship pages regularly for any changes to funding arrangements, eligibility or selection procedures.

About the University of Otago Doctoral Scholarship

The University of Otago Doctoral Scholarship is designed to support students undertaking supervised doctoral research at the University of Otago.

Under the University’s postgraduate scholarship regulations, doctoral scholarships are awarded by the University Council on the recommendation of the Senate and are normally intended for candidates seeking their first doctoral qualification. A candidate may receive only one University of Otago doctoral scholarship.

The scholarship may support students undertaking:

  • Doctor of Philosophy programmes
  • DClinDent
  • Doctor of Musical Arts
  • Doctor of Business Administration
  • Doctor of Education
  • Other eligible doctoral pathways covered by University regulations

The scholarship is highly competitive. Selection is based predominantly on academic performance, research potential and the assessment of the academic department in which the candidate intends to undertake research.

Scholarship Value

For full-time doctoral students, the University of Otago Doctoral Scholarship provides:

NZ$34,128 per year as a living stipend

plus:

A tuition fee waiver at the domestic tuition-fee rate for up to 36 months

The postgraduate research scholarship regulations confirm that the standard full-time doctoral scholarship emolument for 2026 is NZ$34,128, normally paid in monthly instalments once the recipient is fully enrolled.

For professional doctorates such as the DClinDent, DMA, DBA and EdD, the scholarship similarly provides a NZ$34,128 annual stipend and a tuition fee waiver for up to 36 months, although the tuition waiver is capped at the domestic rate.

Students remain responsible for costs not covered by the tuition waiver, including applicable student services fees, insurance and other charges. The regulations specifically state that the scholarship covers the tuition component and that recipients may still be invoiced for remaining fees.

Number of Scholarships Available

The University states that up to:

153 University of Otago Doctoral Scholarships may be offered annually.

Availability remains subject to institutional funding decisions and scholarship programme arrangements.

The University is currently reviewing its doctoral scholarship programme, so future scholarship numbers, selection systems or funding arrangements may change.

Applicants should always confirm the latest information on the University of Otago website before submitting an application.

Who Can Apply?

The scholarship primarily supports candidates seeking their first doctoral qualification.

Applicants will normally need to demonstrate:

  • Excellent previous academic performance
  • Strong potential for research
  • Appropriate preparation for doctoral-level study
  • Admission eligibility for the proposed University of Otago doctoral programme
  • A research topic that can be appropriately supervised at the University

Confirmation of a doctoral scholarship is dependent on the candidate being approved for admission to the relevant doctoral programme and successfully completing the enrolment process.

Can International Students Apply?

International PhD candidates should pay particular attention to the University’s fee-status rules.

The current regulations state that, unless otherwise specified, doctoral and research master’s scholarships are open to Domestic Fee Paying Students. However, the same regulations note that international students undertaking PhD study in New Zealand have been eligible to pay domestic PhD tuition fees under New Zealand policy.

The University’s scholarship information consequently describes the main University of Otago Doctoral Scholarship as available to both domestic and international PhD candidates.

International candidates for professional doctorates may also apply, but where they receive a scholarship, the tuition waiver is limited to the domestic fee rate. Any difference between the domestic-rate waiver and applicable international tuition fees would remain the student’s responsibility.

Because the University is currently reviewing doctoral scholarship arrangements, international applicants should check their precise eligibility and fee status before relying on scholarship funding.

How Candidates Are Selected

The University of Otago Doctoral Scholarship is awarded primarily on the basis of academic merit and research potential.

The postgraduate scholarship regulations identify several factors considered during assessment.

1. Academic Record

The University examines the applicant’s previous academic results.

For candidates who have completed a master’s degree combining coursework and a substantial thesis, relevant advanced-level papers and thesis grades may be considered.

Where a candidate does not have a master’s degree containing a thesis, the University may consider advanced-level papers from the applicant’s most relevant qualification.

For applicants whose qualifications were obtained outside the University of Otago, the University calculates an appropriate GPA using relevant academic transcripts.

2. Research Potential

The applicant’s potential for research, or an existing record of research achievement, is an important component of the assessment.

Relevant evidence may include:

  • Previous thesis research
  • Research projects
  • Academic publications
  • Conference participation
  • Research assistantships
  • Relevant professional research
  • Evidence demonstrating the ability to conduct independent academic work

3. Departmental Recommendation

The advice, recommendation or ranking of the relevant Head of Department is also considered.

This makes academic fit important. A strong scholarship application is not simply a collection of high grades. Candidates should also demonstrate that their proposed research fits the expertise and research environment available within the intended department.

4. Academic Division Priorities

The strategic research and institutional priorities of the Academic Division supervising the proposed research may also influence selection.

Duration of the Scholarship

A full-time doctoral scholarship normally has a maximum tenure of:

Three years

or until the thesis is submitted, whichever occurs first.

Continuation of funding is dependent on satisfactory annual progress reports from the department in which the student is registered.

For candidates who have already completed at least two months of doctoral registration at the time the scholarship is awarded, the total funding period may be reduced accordingly.

Full-Time and Part-Time Study

University regulations allow postgraduate research scholarships to be held on either a full-time or approved part-time basis.

Part-time arrangements are generally considered where full-time study is not practically possible and the candidate can demonstrate appropriate preparation for part-time doctoral research.

Approved reasons for moving from full-time to part-time study can include:

  • Health circumstances
  • Significant caregiving responsibilities
  • Certain career-related circumstances

For approved part-time doctoral scholarship recipients, the scholarship period is generally extended while the annual stipend is reduced proportionally.

The standard 2026 part-time doctoral scholarship emolument identified in the regulations is NZ$17,064 per year.

Where Scholarship Recipients Study

During the scholarship period, doctoral candidates are normally expected to undertake their research at:

  • University of Otago, Dunedin
  • University of Otago, Christchurch
  • University of Otago, Wellington

Exceptions may be approved where the research requires access to overseas facilities or opportunities that are essential to the project.

Overseas doctoral scholarship tenure is not normally permitted automatically, although approval may be granted for particular research circumstances.

Employment While Holding the Scholarship

Full-time doctoral scholarship recipients are permitted to undertake some paid employment, but limits apply.

Under the regulations, full-time scholarship recipients may not normally accept more than 500 hours of paid employment over a 12-month period without prior approval from the Scholarships and Prizes Committee.

Part-time scholarship recipients have a corresponding maximum of 1,000 hours over 12 months without prior permission.

Students must ensure that outside work does not interfere with satisfactory progress on their doctorate.

University of Otago employees undertaking their doctoral qualification as part of their employment are not eligible for University of Otago scholarship funding under the general regulations.

Other Scholarships and Additional Funding

The University of Otago offers a wider range of specialised doctoral funding opportunities in addition to the principal University of Otago Doctoral Scholarship.

Examples include:

University of Otago Māori Doctoral Scholarship

This scholarship is specifically available to Māori doctoral candidates.

University of Otago Pacific Islands Doctoral Scholarship

This funding is reserved for doctoral students of indigenous Pacific Island descent.

University of Otago China Scholarship Council Doctoral Scholarship

This pathway is available to eligible PhD candidates supported by the China Scholarship Council under the University’s institutional arrangements.

The regulations indicate that this scholarship can include tuition support for up to four years and supplementary stipend support designed to bring the recipient’s stipend to the equivalent value of the standard University of Otago Doctoral Scholarship.

University of Otago City of Literature PhD Scholarship

This specialised opportunity supports a PhD candidate whose research focuses on literature.

University of Otago Special Health Research Scholarship

This programme supports outstanding graduate students planning careers in health research. Candidates from different academic disciplines may be considered where the proposed PhD research relates to human health.

Other specialised scholarships exist in areas including economics, education, geology, chemistry, experimental science, cancer research and women’s postgraduate research.

Applicants should therefore explore both the general University of Otago Doctoral Scholarship and any discipline-specific scholarship for which they may qualify.

How to Apply

Applications for University of Otago doctoral scholarships are completed online through the eVision student portal.

The general process is:

  1. Apply for admission to an eligible doctoral programme at the University of Otago.
  2. Complete the required doctoral admission information.
  3. Once the admission application is sufficiently complete, an invitation to apply for a scholarship will appear through eVision.
  4. Complete and submit the scholarship application.
  5. Ensure that the relevant academic department completes its assessment.
  6. Wait for consideration in the appropriate scholarship selection round.

The regulations confirm that applications are submitted online and that candidates receive the scholarship invitation after completing the relevant qualification admission application.

Application Deadline and Quarterly Selection Rounds

There is no single annual closing date for the University of Otago Doctoral Scholarship.

Applications may be made throughout the year.

Scholarship applications are currently considered in quarterly rounds held in:

  • March
  • June
  • September
  • November

Applications must be submitted through eVision and have a completed departmental assessment by the first day of the relevant round month.

Therefore, for applicants preparing applications in August 2026, the next practical assessment point is the September 2026 round, for which the application and departmental assessment should be complete by 1 September 2026.

Candidates who cannot complete the necessary requirements in time can prepare for the November round instead.

International Academic Qualifications

Applicants who completed their previous qualifications outside New Zealand or Australia may be required to undergo academic credential assessment depending on the country and qualification concerned.

The University reserves the right to request an external evaluation of international academic qualifications.

However, the scholarship regulations clarify that an external Education Credential Evaluators assessment is not necessarily required simply to establish scholarship eligibility, although it may be required separately by the University’s International Office for admission purposes.

International applicants should therefore distinguish carefully between:

  • Doctoral admission requirements, and
  • Scholarship assessment requirements

Both processes may involve different documentation.

Reapplying for the Scholarship

University of Otago doctoral scholarships are highly competitive, and scholarship selection decisions are normally final.

However, candidates may request permission to reapply if they have significant new material that strengthens their original application.

Examples could include:

  • New academic results
  • Additional research publications
  • Significant new research experience
  • New evidence of academic achievement

Candidates seeking permission to reapply should contact the University of Otago Scholarships Office and provide their name, student ID and evidence of the new material.

Important Funding Review

Prospective applicants should be aware that the University of Otago has announced that it is reviewing its doctoral scholarship programme.

The current scholarship information remains available, but candidates planning future doctoral study should monitor the official University website for updates.

This is particularly important for applicants planning to begin their doctorate in a later academic period, since scholarship values, allocation mechanisms, eligibility or selection procedures could change.

Contact Information

For questions relating to postgraduate scholarships, applicants can contact:

University of Otago Scholarships Office

Email: scholarships@otago.ac.nz

Telephone: 0800 80 80 98

Applicants should also consult the official University of Otago scholarship pages for the latest information on doctoral funding and specialised scholarship opportunities.

Conclusion

The University of Otago Doctoral Scholarship 2026 provides significant financial support for high-achieving doctoral candidates seeking to undertake research at one of New Zealand’s leading universities.

With a NZ$34,128 annual stipend, a domestic-rate tuition fee waiver for up to three years and up to 153 scholarships potentially offered annually, the programme represents an important funding route for prospective PhD researchers.

Applications can be submitted throughout the year through eVision and are assessed in quarterly rounds in March, June, September and November. Selection is strongly based on academic merit, research potential, departmental recommendation and alignment with the University’s research priorities.

International PhD applicants may also be eligible, subject to doctoral admission and applicable domestic-fee status arrangements, while international professional doctorate candidates should pay particular attention to the domestic-rate cap on tuition support.

Because the University is currently reviewing its doctoral scholarship programme, applicants should verify the latest funding arrangements before applying.

For more information and to apply, visit the official University of Otago Doctoral Scholarship website.

To discover more global scholarship opportunities, VISIT HERE.
